purpose: Name the ways a death-vocabulary archive can accidentally steal, aestheticize, flatten, or commercialize community practices.

risks.name: beautiful outsider summary
risks.description: A surface becomes poetic and portable while deleting authority, obligation, cost, law, grief, and family specificity.
risks.mitigation: Keep source, authority, local-law, and nonclaim text visible.

risks.name: ritual tourism
risks.description: Readers consume death practices as exotic scenes rather than community-governed relations.
risks.mitigation: No interior ritual details; no image-seeking; no decorative borrowing language.

risks.name: diaspora flattening
risks.description: US/UK English-language summaries are mistaken for global tradition authority.
risks.mitigation: Mark geography, denomination, lineage, diaspora adaptation, and source type.

risks.name: commercial-source capture
risks.description: Funeral-industry pages supply convenient summaries shaped by service sales.
risks.mitigation: Weight commercial summaries low and route to families/tradition holders.

risks.name: forbidden equivalence
risks.description: Different traditions are rendered as interchangeable comfort rituals.
risks.mitigation: Preserve terms, do not universalize, and include contrast/variant fields.
